# Student Depression Analysis using Statistical Inference and Modelling in R
# ITS66804 Group Assignment | Kaggle Student Depression Dataset

# Install any required package that is not already available, then load it.
required_packages <- c(
  "tidyverse", "psych", "ggplot2", "car", "lmtest", "ResourceSelection",
  "pROC", "caret", "broom", "DescTools", "corrplot", "nortest",
  "effectsize", "PerformanceAnalytics", "reshape2"
)

install_and_load <- function(package_name) {
  if (!requireNamespace(package_name, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(package_name, dependencies = TRUE)
  }
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(package_name, character.only = TRUE))
}

invisible(lapply(required_packages, install_and_load))

# Reproducibility and consistent reporting settings.
set.seed(66804)
options(scipen = 999, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
alpha <- 0.05

# User-facing output directory. All tables and publication-quality figures go here.

# Professional graph style used by all newly generated figures.
project_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#163A5F", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# A common interpretation printer required after every inferential procedure.
print_inference <- function(hypothesis, p_value, interpretation, practical_conclusion,
                            test_name = "Statistical test") {
  decision <- ifelse(is.na(p_value), "Decision unavailable",
                     ifelse(p_value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0"))
  cat("\n----------------------------------------------------\n")
  cat(test_name, "\n")
  cat("Hypothesis: ", hypothesis, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("P-value: ", ifelse(is.na(p_value), "NA", format.pval(p_value, digits = 4)), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("Decision: ", decision, " at alpha = ", alpha, ".\n", sep = "")
  cat("Interpretation: ", interpretation, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("Practical conclusion: ", practical_conclusion, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("----------------------------------------------------\n")
  invisible(decision)
}

# Shapiro-Wilk is sensitive with large samples. This helper samples at most 5,000
# observations, which is the test's R limit, and returns a usable p-value.
safe_shapiro <- function(x, max_n = 5000) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) < 3 || length(unique(x)) < 3) return(NA_real_)
  if (length(x) > max_n) x <- sample(x, max_n)
  tryCatch(shapiro.test(x)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

  ux <- na.omit(unique(x))
  if (length(ux) == 0) return(NA)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

# IQR method: values below Q1 - 1.5*IQR or above Q3 + 1.5*IQR are outliers.
detect_outliers <- function(x) {
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  IQR_val <- Q3 - Q1
  lower <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_val
  upper <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_val
  sum(x < lower | x > upper, na.rm = TRUE)
}

numeric_vars <- c("Age", "Academic.Pressure", "CGPA",
                  "Study.Satisfaction", "Work.Study.Hours", "Financial.Stress")
outlier_counts_before <- sapply(df[numeric_vars], detect_outliers)

                          IQR_Outliers_Before = as.integer(outlier_counts_before))
cat("IQR outlier counts before treatment:\n")
print(outlier_summary)

# Winsorise numeric values to the IQR fences. The supplied EDA then retains its
# original Age treatment exactly as provided, as requested.
cap_outliers <- function(x) {
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  IQR_val <- Q3 - Q1
  lower <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_val
  upper <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_val
  x[x < lower] <- lower
  x[x > upper] <- upper
  return(x)
}

####################################################
# SECTION 6: RESEARCH OBJECTIVES
####################################################

# General Objective:
# To examine factors associated with depression among university students using
# statistical inference and multivariable logistic regression.
#
# Specific Objectives:
# 1. Describe students' demographic, academic, lifestyle, and mental-health data.
# 2. Test whether selected categorical and numerical predictors differ by depression.
# 3. Model the probability of depression using all specified predictor variables.
# 4. Evaluate predictive accuracy and identify the most influential predictors.
#
# Research Questions:
# 1. Are academic pressure, financial stress, sleep duration, CGPA, family history,
#    and gender associated with depression?
# 2. Which student characteristics independently predict depression?
# 3. How accurately can the fitted model classify depression status?

####################################################
# SECTION 7: HYPOTHESES
####################################################

# H01: Academic Pressure has no significant relationship with Depression.
# H11: Academic Pressure has a significant relationship with Depression.
# H02: Financial Stress has no significant relationship with Depression.
# H12: Financial Stress has a significant relationship with Depression.
# H03: Sleep Duration has no significant relationship with Depression.
# H13: Sleep Duration has a significant relationship with Depression.
# H04: CGPA has no significant relationship with Depression.
# H14: CGPA has a significant relationship with Depression.
# H05: Family History of Mental Illness has no significant relationship with Depression.
# H15: Family History of Mental Illness has a significant relationship with Depression.
# H06: Gender has no significant relationship with Depression.
# H16: Gender has a significant relationship with Depression.

####################################################
# SECTION 8: ASSUMPTION CHECKING
####################################################

continuous_tests <- c("Age", "CGPA", "Academic.Pressure", "Study.Satisfaction",
                      "Financial.Stress", "Work.Study.Hours")
assumption_results <- list()

for (variable in continuous_tests) {
  cat("\nAssumption checks for", variable, "by Depression\n")
  group_p <- tapply(df[[variable]], df$Depression, safe_shapiro)
  print(group_p)
  for (group_name in names(group_p)) {
    if (is.na(group_p[[group_name]])) {
      cat(group_name, ": Normality could not be assessed.\n")
    } else if (group_p[[group_name]] > alpha) {
      cat(group_name, ": Data is normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk p > 0.05).\n")
    } else {
      cat(group_name, ": Data is NOT normally distributed (Shapiro-Wilk p <= 0.05).\n")
    }
  }
  lev <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(variable, "~ Depression")), data = df)
  lev_p <- lev["Pr(>F)"][1, 1]
  print(lev)
  if (lev_p > alpha) {
    cat("Levene test: Homogeneity of variance is satisfied.\n")
  } else {
    cat("Levene test: Homogeneity of variance is NOT satisfied.\n")
  }
  assumption_results[[variable]] <- tibble(
    Variable = variable, Shapiro_No = unname(group_p["No"]),
    Shapiro_Yes = unname(group_p["Yes"]), Levene_p = lev_p
  )
  
  qq_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(sample = .data[[variable]])) +
    stat_qq(colour = "#2166AC", alpha = 0.45) + stat_qq_line(colour = "#B2182B") +
    facet_wrap(~Depression) + labs(title = paste("Q-Q Plot:", variable, "by Depression"),
                                   x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles") + project_theme
  ggsave(paste0("QQPlot_", variable, ".png"), qq_plot, width = 7, height = 4.8, dpi = 300)
}
assumption_results <- bind_rows(assumption_results)
####################################################
# SECTION 9: CHI-SQUARE TESTS
####################################################

chi_variables <- c("Gender", "Sleep.Duration", "Dietary.Habits",
                   "Family.History.of.Mental.Illness",
                   "Have.you.ever.had.suicidal.thoughts..", "Degree")
chi_labels <- c("Gender", "Sleep Duration", "Dietary Habits", "Family History",
                "Suicidal Thoughts", "Degree")
chi_results <- list()

for (i in seq_along(chi_variables)) {
  variable <- chi_variables[i]
  label <- chi_labels[i]
  observed <- table(df[[variable]], df$Depression)
  chi_test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(observed))
  cat("\nChi-square test:", label, "vs Depression\nObserved table:\n")
  print(observed)
  cat("Expected table:\n")
  print(round(chi_test$expected, 2))
  cat("Chi-square statistic:", round(unname(chi_test$statistic), 4), "\n")
  cat("Degrees of freedom:", unname(chi_test$parameter), "\n")
  cat("P-value:", format.pval(chi_test$p.value, digits = 4), "\n")
  interpretation <- ifelse(chi_test$p.value < alpha,
                           paste(label, "has a statistically significant association with Depression."),
                           paste(label, "does not have a statistically significant association with Depression."))
  print_inference(paste("H0:", label, "and Depression are independent."), chi_test$p.value,
                  interpretation, "Interpret association alongside effect size and sample context.",
                  paste("Chi-square test:", label, "vs Depression"))
  chi_results[[i]] <- tibble(Variable = label, Chi_Square = unname(chi_test$statistic),
                             Degrees_of_Freedom = unname(chi_test$parameter), P_Value = chi_test$p.value,
                             Decision = ifelse(chi_test$p.value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0"),
                             Minimum_Expected_Count = min(chi_test$expected))
}
chi_results <- bind_rows(chi_results)
####################################################
# SECTION 10: INDEPENDENT SAMPLES T-TEST
####################################################

ttest_variables <- c("Age", "CGPA", "Academic.Pressure", "Study.Satisfaction",
                     "Financial.Stress", "Work.Study.Hours")
ttest_labels <- c("Age", "CGPA", "Academic Pressure", "Study Satisfaction",
                  "Financial Stress", "Study Hours")
ttest_results <- list()

for (i in seq_along(ttest_variables)) {
  variable <- ttest_variables[i]
  label <- ttest_labels[i]
  p_by_group <- tapply(df[[variable]], df$Depression, safe_shapiro)
  normality_ok <- all(!is.na(p_by_group) & p_by_group > alpha)
  levene_p <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(variable, "~ Depression")), data = df)["Pr(>F)"][1, 1]
  group_means <- df %>% group_by(Depression) %>% summarise(Mean = mean(.data[[variable]]), .groups = "drop")
  
  if (normality_ok) {
    test <- t.test(as.formula(paste(variable, "~ Depression")), data = df,
                   var.equal = levene_p > alpha)
    method <- ifelse(levene_p > alpha, "Independent samples t-test", "Welch t-test")
    statistic <- unname(test$statistic)
    df_test <- unname(test$parameter)
    effect <- effectsize::cohens_d(as.formula(paste(variable, "~ Depression")), data = df)$Cohens_d[1]
  } else {
    test <- wilcox.test(as.formula(paste(variable, "~ Depression")), data = df, exact = FALSE)
    method <- "Mann-Whitney U test"
    statistic <- unname(test$statistic)
    df_test <- NA_real_
    effect <- NA_real_
  }
  p_value <- test$p.value
  interpretation <- ifelse(p_value < alpha,
                           paste("Mean/rank", label, "differs significantly between depression groups."),
                           paste("There is no statistically significant difference in", label, "between depression groups."))
  cat("\n", method, "for", label, "\n", sep = "")
  print(group_means)
  print_inference(paste("H0: The", label, "distribution is equal for No and Yes Depression."),
                  p_value, interpretation, "Use the group summaries to describe the direction of the difference.", method)
  ttest_results[[i]] <- tibble(Variable = label, Test = method, Statistic = statistic,
                               Degrees_of_Freedom = df_test, P_Value = p_value, Effect_Size_Cohens_d = effect,
                               Decision = ifelse(p_value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0"))
}
ttest_results <- bind_rows(ttest_results)
####################################################
# SECTION 11: ONE-WAY ANOVA
####################################################

anova_specs <- list(
  list(outcome = "CGPA", group = "Sleep.Duration", label = "CGPA by Sleep Duration"),
  list(outcome = "Academic.Pressure", group = "Dietary.Habits", label = "Academic Pressure by Dietary Habits"),
  list(outcome = "Financial.Stress", group = "Degree", label = "Financial Stress by Degree")
)
anova_results <- list()

for (i in seq_along(anova_specs)) {
  spec <- anova_specs[[i]]
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste(spec$outcome, "~", spec$group))
  anova_model <- aov(model_formula, data = df)
  anova_table <- summary(anova_model)[[1]]
  p_value <- anova_table[1, "Pr(>F)"]
  cat("\nANOVA:", spec$label, "\n")
  print(anova_table)
  interpretation <- ifelse(p_value < alpha,
                           paste("At least one", spec$group, "group has a different mean", spec$outcome, "."),
                           paste("No evidence of a difference in mean", spec$outcome, "across", spec$group, "groups."))
  print_inference(paste("H0: Mean", spec$outcome, "is equal across", spec$group, "groups."),
                  p_value, interpretation, "ANOVA identifies an overall difference; inspect Tukey comparisons when significant.",
                  paste("One-way ANOVA:", spec$label))
  if (!is.na(p_value) && p_value < alpha) {
    cat("Tukey HSD post-hoc comparisons:\n")
    print(TukeyHSD(anova_model))
  }
  anova_results[[i]] <- tibble(Analysis = spec$label, F_Statistic = anova_table[1, "F value"],
                               Numerator_DF = anova_table[1, "Df"], Denominator_DF = anova_table[2, "Df"],
                               P_Value = p_value, Decision = ifelse(p_value < alpha, "Reject H0", "Fail to reject H0"))
}
anova_results <- bind_rows(anova_results)
####################################################
# SECTION 12: LOGISTIC REGRESSION
####################################################

# Create a numeric outcome for glm while retaining the labelled Depression factor.
df <- df %>% mutate(Depression_Binary = ifelse(Depression == "Yes", 1, 0))
predictor_variables <- c("Age", "Gender", "Academic.Pressure", "Study.Satisfaction",
                         "CGPA", "Work.Study.Hours", "Sleep.Duration", "Dietary.Habits", "Degree",
                         "Financial.Stress", "Family.History.of.Mental.Illness",
                         "Have.you.ever.had.suicidal.thoughts..")
model_formula <- as.formula(paste("Depression_Binary ~", paste(predictor_variables, collapse = " + ")))
logistic_model <- glm(model_formula, data = df, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

cat("\nLogistic regression model summary:\n")
print(summary(logistic_model))
regression_coefficients <- broom::tidy(logistic_model, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Significant = ifelse(p.value < alpha, "Yes", "No"))
print(regression_coefficients)

odds_ratios <- regression_coefficients %>%
  transmute(Term = term, Odds_Ratio = exp(estimate), CI_Lower = exp(conf.low),
            CI_Upper = exp(conf.high), P_Value = p.value,
            Significant = Significant) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(log(Odds_Ratio))))
cat("\nOdds ratios with 95% confidence intervals:\n")
print(odds_ratios)

for (row in seq_len(nrow(regression_coefficients))) {
  term_name <- regression_coefficients$term[row]
  if (term_name != "(Intercept)") {
    p_value <- regression_coefficients$p.value[row]
    direction <- ifelse(regression_coefficients$estimate[row] > 0, "increases", "decreases")
    print_inference(paste("H0: Regression coefficient for", term_name, "equals zero."), p_value,
                    ifelse(p_value < alpha, paste(term_name, "is a significant predictor of Depression."),
                           paste(term_name, "is not a statistically significant predictor after adjustment.")),
                    paste("Holding other variables constant, this predictor", direction, "the odds of depression."),
                    paste("Logistic regression coefficient:", term_name))
  }
}
####################################################
# SECTION 13: MULTICOLLINEARITY
####################################################

vif_raw <- car::vif(logistic_model)
if (is.matrix(vif_raw)) {
  vif_results <- as.data.frame(vif_raw) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("Variable") %>%
    mutate(Adjusted_VIF = GVIF^(1 / (2 * Df)), Interpretation = case_when(
      Adjusted_VIF < 5 ~ "Low multicollinearity", Adjusted_VIF < 10 ~ "Moderate multicollinearity",
      TRUE ~ "High multicollinearity"))
} else {
  vif_results <- tibble(Variable = names(vif_raw), VIF = as.numeric(vif_raw)) %>%
    mutate(Adjusted_VIF = VIF, Interpretation = case_when(
      VIF < 5 ~ "Low multicollinearity", VIF < 10 ~ "Moderate multicollinearity",
      TRUE ~ "High multicollinearity"))
}
cat("\nVariance Inflation Factors:\n")
print(vif_results)
apply(vif_results, 1, function(x) cat(x[["Variable"]], ":", x[["Interpretation"]], "(adjusted VIF =", round(as.numeric(x[["Adjusted_VIF"]]), 2), ")\n"))
####################################################
# SECTION 14: GOODNESS OF FIT
####################################################

predicted_probability <- predict(logistic_model, type = "response")
hl_test <- ResourceSelection::hoslem.test(df$Depression_Binary, predicted_probability, g = 10)
nagelkerke_r2 <- DescTools::PseudoR2(logistic_model, which = "Nagelkerke")
model_aic <- AIC(logistic_model)
model_bic <- BIC(logistic_model)

cat("\nHosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test:\n")
print(hl_test)
print_inference("H0: The logistic model fits the observed data adequately.", hl_test$p.value,
                ifelse(hl_test$p.value > alpha, "No evidence of lack of fit; calibration is acceptable.",
                       "Evidence of lack of fit; interpret predictions cautiously."),
                "Use calibration, discrimination, and classification measures together.", "Hosmer-Lemeshow test")
cat("Nagelkerke pseudo R-squared:", round(nagelkerke_r2, 4), "\n")
cat("AIC:", round(model_aic, 2), " | BIC:", round(model_bic, 2), "\n")
cat("Lower AIC/BIC values indicate a more parsimonious fit only when models are compared on the same data.\n")
####################################################
# SECTION 15: PREDICTION
####################################################

predicted_class <- factor(ifelse(predicted_probability >= 0.50, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
actual_class <- factor(df$Depression, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
confusion <- caret::confusionMatrix(predicted_class, actual_class, positive = "Yes")
cat("\nConfusion matrix:\n")
print(confusion$table)
cat("\nClassification performance:\n")
print(confusion$overall)
print(confusion$byClass)

precision <- unname(confusion$byClass["Precision"])
recall <- unname(confusion$byClass["Recall"])
specificity <- unname(confusion$byClass["Specificity"])
f1_score <- unname(confusion$byClass["F1"])
accuracy <- unname(confusion$overall["Accuracy"])
kappa <- unname(confusion$overall["Kappa"])
performance_results <- tibble(Accuracy = accuracy, Precision = precision, Recall = recall,
                              Specificity = specificity, Sensitivity = recall, F1_Score = f1_score, Kappa = kappa)
print(performance_results)
print_inference("H0: The model performs no better than chance classification.", NA_real_,
                "Classification measures describe in-sample predictive performance; they are not a hypothesis test.",
                paste("Accuracy is", round(100 * accuracy, 2), "%; validate on new data before operational use."),
                "Prediction performance")
####################################################
# SECTION 16: ROC CURVE
####################################################

roc_object <- pROC::roc(response = actual_class, predictor = predicted_probability,
                        levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<")
auc_value <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_object))
auc_interpretation <- dplyr::case_when(
  auc_value >= 0.90 ~ "excellent discrimination",
  auc_value >= 0.80 ~ "good discrimination",
  auc_value >= 0.70 ~ "acceptable discrimination",
  auc_value >= 0.60 ~ "poor discrimination",
  TRUE ~ "no useful discrimination"
)
cat("AUC:", round(auc_value, 4), "-", auc_interpretation, "\n")
print_inference("H0: AUC equals 0.50 (no discrimination).", NA_real_,
                paste("The model has", auc_interpretation, "with AUC =", round(auc_value, 3), "."),
                "A higher AUC means better separation of students with and without depression.", "ROC analysis")

roc_plot <- ggroc(roc_object, colour = "#2166AC", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.62, y = 0.10, label = paste("AUC =", round(auc_value, 3)), size = 4.5) +
  labs(title = "ROC Curve: Logistic Regression Model", x = "1 - Specificity", y = "Sensitivity") + project_theme
ggsave("ROC_Curve_Publication_Quality.png", roc_plot, width = 7, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
####################################################
# SECTION 17: VARIABLE IMPORTANCE
####################################################

# Absolute Wald z statistics rank terms by adjusted evidence in the fitted model.
variable_importance <- regression_coefficients %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  transmute(Variable = term, Estimate = estimate, Odds_Ratio = exp(estimate),
            Wald_Z = statistic, P_Value = p.value, Importance = abs(statistic),
            Significant = Significant) %>% arrange(desc(Importance))
cat("\nVariable importance table (most to least important):\n")
print(variable_importance)

importance_plot <- variable_importance %>% slice_head(n = 20) %>%
  mutate(Variable = reorder(Variable, Importance)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Variable, y = Importance, fill = Significant)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() + scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yes" = "#B2182B", "No" = "#92B6D5")) +
  labs(title = "Variable Importance in the Logistic Regression Model", x = NULL,
       y = "Absolute Wald z Statistic", fill = "Significant") + project_theme
ggsave("Variable_Importance_Plot.png", importance_plot, width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
####################################################
# SECTION 18: PUBLICATION QUALITY GRAPHS
####################################################

# Predicted probability by observed depression status.
probability_plot <- tibble(Depression = actual_class, Probability = predicted_probability) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Depression, y = Probability, fill = Depression)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75, outlier.alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.08, size = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "#4CAF50", "Yes" = "#E57373")) +
  labs(title = "Predicted Probability of Depression by Observed Status", x = "Observed Depression", y = "Predicted Probability") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") + project_theme
ggsave("Logistic_Regression_Probability_Plot.png", probability_plot, width = 7, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)

# Adjusted odds ratios and confidence intervals for interpretable model terms.
or_plot_data <- odds_ratios %>% filter(Term != "(Intercept)", is.finite(Odds_Ratio),
                                       is.finite(CI_Lower), is.finite(CI_Upper)) %>% slice_head(n = 25) %>% mutate(Term = reorder(Term, Odds_Ratio))
odds_ratio_plot <- ggplot(or_plot_data, aes(x = Term, y = Odds_Ratio, ymin = CI_Lower, ymax = CI_Upper, colour = Significant)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_pointrange() + coord_flip() + scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Yes" = "#B2182B", "No" = "#2166AC")) +
  labs(title = "Adjusted Odds Ratios with 95% Confidence Intervals", x = NULL,
       y = "Odds Ratio (log scale)", colour = "Significant") + project_theme
ggsave("Odds_Ratio_Plot.png", odds_ratio_plot, width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)

# Distribution of fitted probabilities by predicted class.
prediction_distribution_plot <- tibble(Predicted_Class = predicted_class, Probability = predicted_probability) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Probability, fill = Predicted_Class)) + geom_density(alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.50, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "#4CAF50", "Yes" = "#E57373")) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Predicted Depression Probabilities", x = "Predicted Probability", y = "Density", fill = "Predicted Class") + project_theme
ggsave("Prediction_Distribution_Plot.png", prediction_distribution_plot, width = 7, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)

# Deviance residuals identify systematic model misfit or unusual observations.
residual_plot <- tibble(Fitted = predicted_probability, Deviance_Residual = residuals(logistic_model, type = "deviance")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Fitted, y = Deviance_Residual)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.18, colour = "#2166AC") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#B2182B") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "#EF6C00") +
  labs(title = "Deviance Residuals versus Fitted Probabilities", x = "Fitted Probability", y = "Deviance Residual") + project_theme
ggsave("Residual_Plot.png", residual_plot, width = 7, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
####################################################
# SECTION 19: AUTOMATIC INTERPRETATION
####################################################

# Each inferential section above calls print_inference() immediately after its
# test. The following concise model summary completes the automated narrative.
significant_terms <- variable_importance %>% filter(P_Value < alpha) %>% pull(Variable)
cat("\nAUTOMATIC MODEL INTERPRETATION\n")
cat("Hypothesis: All adjusted logistic regression coefficients equal zero.\n")
cat("P-value: Individual coefficient p-values are printed in Section 12.\n")
cat("Decision: ", ifelse(length(significant_terms) > 0, "At least one adjusted predictor is significant.", "No adjusted predictor is significant."), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Interpretation: ", length(significant_terms), "model term(s) are significant at alpha = 0.05.\n", sep = "")
cat("Practical conclusion: The model should support understanding and screening, not clinical diagnosis.\n")
####################################################
# SECTION 20: EXPORT RESULTS
####################################################

# Export requested submission tables with clear, consistent filenames.
write.csv(descriptive_stats, "Descriptive Statistics.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(chi_results, "ChiSquareResults.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(ttest_results, "TTestResults.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(anova_results, "ANOVAResults.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(regression_coefficients, "RegressionCoefficients.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(odds_ratios, "OddsRatios.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(as.data.frame.matrix(confusion$table) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("Predicted"),
          "ConfusionMatrix.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(performance_results %>% mutate(AUC = auc_value, AIC = model_aic, BIC = model_bic,
                                         Nagelkerke_R2 = nagelkerke_r2, Hosmer_Lemeshow_P = hl_test$p.value),
          "ModelPerformance.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(variable_importance, "VariableImportance.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(tibble(Observed_Depression = actual_class, Predicted_Probability = predicted_probability,
                 Predicted_Class = predicted_class), "PredictedProbabilities.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(assumption_results, "AssumptionCheckResults.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(outlier_summary, "OutlierSummary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n====================================================\n")
cat("ANALYSIS COMPLETE\n")
cat("All requested CSV tables and 300 dpi PNG figures were saved to:C:\users\karya\IdeaProjects\group project.java\out\artifacts\group_project_java_jar\n")
cat(normalizePath(results_dir, winslash = "/"), "\n")
cat("====================================================\n")
